…ietnamworks, topcv, superjob (issue #29 R-V3..R-V12)

Each platform ships a data-only descriptor: URLs, auth mode, evidence
observed on the public internet, an ordered read plan and update groups
guarded by the canonical paths they write. Every step carries a
confidence level (verified/documented/draft) so the parts still based
on public knowledge are labelled rather than hidden, and validation
fails CI when a plan writes a path it never reads back, references a
missing mapper, or claims 'verified' without evidence.

…able sinks (issue #29 R-V13)

Every step is logged with its selector, fallbacks, timing and values,
and every snapshot is fingerprinted structurally so a layout change on
a platform surfaces as a markup.changed event with the dropped test ids
named, instead of a silently empty CV. Events stream to memory, JSON
Lines and the links store; personal data is redacted by default so a
run log can be attached to a bug report.

… #29 R-V14)

Interprets a platform's declarative read/update plans against a
browser-commander instance: selector fallbacks, canonical path
assignment with type coercion, JSON mappers, markup snapshots and
screenshots, all reported through the run telemetry. Optional misses
become warnings, required misses fail with a typed error, and a
redirect to a login page is classified as login-required so an expired
session is never mistaken for an empty CV.

Tested with a fake commander that executes the real extractors against
the captured Habr Career markup, so the whole read path is covered
without a browser.

commits.messageBody:
Adds the browser session factory (browser-commander + playwright as
optional dependencies, persistent per-platform profile, typed error
when they are absent) and the facade the CLI, server and SPA share:
readCvFrom, readAllCvs, loadStoredCvs, compareAllCvs, diffAllCvs,
updateCvOn and syncCvAcross. Snapshots persist as cv:<platform> links
in links notation and every run's telemetry lands in the same store.

Reconciliation now travels both ways: applyFlatChanges/cvFromFlat
invert the keyed flattening, so a comparison plan can be materialised
into the CV the runner writes back, merging records by identity rather
than by position.

…sue #29)

The source registry links every job board to its CV plan, and the SPA
imports that registry. The lazy `import('../cv/index.js')` in the CV
bridge was still followed by esbuild, so `npm run build:web` — and with
it the Pages deployment — failed on `playwright`, `node:os` and
`node:fs/promises`.

Hold the specifier in a constant so no bundler can follow it, and guard
the call with a typed `CvRuntimeUnavailableError` that points browser
callers at `/api/cv`. `js/tests/web-bundle.test.js` walks the SPA import
graph on disk (Node/Bun/Deno alike) and fails on any node:/playwright
edge or on the CV runtime reappearing.

…ue #29 R-V18)

A single screen for the loop the issue asks for: list every supported
platform with its plan confidence and last snapshot, read the live CVs
through the local browser session, show the conflicting fields side by
side, plan a sync and apply it only on an explicit click. The telemetry
panel replays the counts and problems each run recorded, so a broken
selector is visible in the UI and not only in a server log.

- js/src/web/cv-view.js: `CvScreen` is pure and `CvView` adds the state
  hook, so the whole surface renders server-side in tests.
- js/src/web/dom.js: `api.cv*` passthroughs with honest
  `server-required` answers when no server is reachable.
- nav-items/views/connection-guides: the screen is a first-class nav
  surface with its own guide.
- locales en/ru/zh/hi: `nav.cv`, the `cv.*` block and `guide.cv.*` in
  full key parity.
- js/tests/cv-web.test.js: 12 render assertions across every locale.

commits.messageBody:
The plans are declarative, so the markup they expect can be derived
from the plans themselves: `js/tests/helpers/markup-fixture.js` turns
every selector back into the smallest DOM that satisfies it, and
`js/tests/e2e-cv-browser.mjs` serves those pages at the platform's own
URLs through Playwright request interception. That runs the shipped
path — openBrowserSession, browser-commander, the plan runner, the
telemetry sink — against real Chromium for all seven platforms: read,
drift detection and every update group.

The e2e is opt-in (`RUN_BROWSER_E2E=1 npm run test:e2e:cv`) and skips
when playwright or browser-commander are absent, so the generator gets
a browser-free unit test of its own to keep it honest in CI.

…-V20)

`cv-sync` was all-or-nothing: every writable field a platform accepted
was written. A user who only wants to fix a headline had no way to say
so, and the docs promised a filter that did not exist.

- `syncCvAcross({ paths, groups })` filters the reconciled changes and
  reports a supported-but-unselected field as `deselected`, which is a
  different fact from the platform having no editor for it
  (`unsupported`).
- `cv-sync --paths=basics.headline --groups=intro` on the CLI, and the
  same two keys on `POST /api/cv/sync`.

commits.messageBody:
`serverFetch` fetched a relative path and parsed whatever came back,
which broke the SPA in the two configurations the docs describe:

- Connected cross-origin (GitHub Pages or a file:// page talking to a
  server on 127.0.0.1), every `/api/*` call went to the page's own
  host instead of the discovered server. Now the path is resolved
  against the discovered origin.
- Against the Rust backend, `/api/cv/*` answers 404 with a JSON error
  body, so `{error: 'unknown route'}` reached the screens as data —
  the CV screen then threw inside its effect and rendered nothing at
  all. A non-2xx or non-JSON reply is now the same as being offline,
  which is what every caller's `?? fallback` already assumed.

The CV screen says so instead of showing an empty table, and a thrown
error lands in the same failure list as a platform failure rather than
in an unhandled rejection.
commits.messageHeadline: fix(web): make a backend without the CV routes visible (issue #29 R-V22)

  how to run the whole thing.
- `docs/REQUIREMENTS.md`: section V (R-V1..R-V22) and the three new
  connector rows (Naukri, VietnamWorks, TopCV).
- `docs/USER-GUIDE.md`: a task-shaped section for the `cv-*` commands,
  including what each failure code means.
- `docs/SERVER-PARITY.md`: the seven `/api/cv/*` routes, why three of
  them cannot be ported while the Rust crate is `std`-only, and the
  refreshed totals.
- The inherited case study about the *pipeline template's* issue #29
  moves to `docs/case-studies/pipeline-template-issue-29/` so the
  folder name stops claiming to be about this one.
